canonical.definition: The hydraulic filtration domain covers particle cleanliness control in hydraulic circuits protecting proportional valves, piston pumps, and actuators from particle-induced wear, spool stiction, and flow degradation caused by contamination above ISO 4406 target codes.
canonical.systems: Mobile hydraulic systems (excavators, loaders, cranes), stationary hydraulic power units, servo and proportional valve circuits, hydrostatic transmission systems
canonical.failure_impact: Particle contamination above ISO 4406 17/15/12 → spool valve silting in proportional valves (1–4 µm silt) → erratic actuator response → valve replacement | Hard particles → piston pump barrel wear → internal leakage → system pressure loss | Particle contamination accounts for 70–80% of premature hydraulic component failures.
canonical.related_standards: ISO 16889: Multi-pass filter efficiency test methodology (Beta ratio) | ISO 4406: Particle cleanliness code classification; target 17/15/12 to 16/14/11 | NFPA T2.14: Hydraulic fluid power contamination control guidelines
canonical.related_technologies: NANOFORCE: High-Beta hydraulic filter elements for inline and return-line applications targeting ISO 4406 16/14/11 to 17/15/12 cleanliness
canonical.industrial_role: Hydraulic filtration maintains the cleanliness codes required for proportional valve and piston pump reliability — particle contamination above cleanliness targets is the leading cause of unplanned hydraulic system downtime in mobile and industrial equipment.
